transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
New York Democratic Governor Kathy Hochul has appointed State Attorney General Letitia
James to be special prosecutor to oversee investigation of Cornell University gang rape
allegations.
Hochul said she had lost faith in the local prosecutor's ability to handle the case.
NPR confirmed the alleged victim told police clearly in 2024 that she was raped.
This contradicts a statement from local prosecutor Matthew Van Houten, who said that the woman
initially described the incident as consensual.
Attorneys for Christa Pike, the woman who received two lethal injections in Tennessee yesterday
and still lived, were told she is in critical condition.
One of her attorneys, Stephen Farrell, said she had a blood condition that makes it difficult
to administer injections.
We presented evidence that due to her blood condition, venous access would be difficult,
and that this type of prolonged execution that she didn't want to happen would happen.
Tennessee Republican Governor Bill Lee has put executions in the state on hold and called
for a third-party review to determine what caused the failed execution.
Pike's attorneys are calling for the governor to commute her death sentence.
In a new letter, thousands of doctors are encouraging senators not to confirm Dr. Heidi
Overton to be the next FDA commissioner, and PR Sydney Lupkin reports.
A letter to senators co-signed by more than 2,500 physicians says Overton is unfit to
lead the FDA.
It came from the committee to protect health care, which is a left-leaning national advocacy
group of doctors and other health care workers.
The letter cited Overton's "dangerous record on vaccines and extremist anti-abortion advocacy."
The group said her record made them believe she wouldn't uphold the FDA's rigorous evidence-based
standards if given the top job.
Overton's confirmation hearing before a Senate health committee took place last week.
A vote likely won't happen until Congress is back in session in November after the midterms.
Sydney Lupkin, NPR News.
The tight U.S. Senate race in Maine could decide who controls Congress.
Republican Susan Collins has won the state five times, NPR's Luke Garrett spoke to voters.
Both Collins and her Democratic challenger Troy Jackson hail from Arista County, a rural
region that borders Canada.
Here, the chief political concerns are the prices of gas and heating oil.
Sabrina Haney sells farmed vegetables in Caribou, Maine.
Our economy sucks right now.
The gas prices need to go down, the fuel prices need to go down.
They just need to help us out.
And over in Fort Kent, Maine, Brandon Goding owns a local movie theater.
With heating oil prices up 74 percent since last year, he's just not sure if he can keep
it warm.
I'm definitely scared for the winter.
My tank's full right now from the summer, and we do have heat pumps, but they're older.
They only do so much in these big open spaces.
Goding says he'll vote for the candidate that brings down the price of heating oil.
Luke Garrett, NPR News, Arista County, Maine.
From Washington, you're listening to NPR News.
A judge in Washington has agreed to permanently dismiss a criminal case charging a former
Olympian with vandalizing the reflecting pool in Washington, D.C.
David Hearn's lawyers say the Trump administration has continued to falsely accuse the Maryland
resident of vandalizing the reflecting pool despite prosecutors' decision to drop the case.
The Trump administration has restored specialized suicide prevention service for LGBTQ+ youth
through the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline, NPR's Ritu Chatterjee reports.
The 988 helpline had received nearly 1.3 million contacts from LGBTQ+ youth over three years
before it was shut down.
Those contacts included calls, texts, and online chats.
In January of this year, the U.S. Senate passed a bipartisan bill to fund the federal health
department that also mandated the restoration of the specialized service on 988.
Democratic Senator Tammy Baldwin of Wisconsin is a lead sponsor of that legislation.
I hope the restoration will restore trust and faith that people should indeed reach
out to 988.
LGBTQ+ youth can once again access specialized crisis support tailored for them by dialing
988 and then pressing option 3.
Ritu Chatterjee, NPR News.
Four astronauts have arrived at the International Space Station following an express eight-hour
flight.
Although their space station stay will last a long six months, the flight launched by SpaceX
was the quickest yet for any U.S. entity.
I'm Rylan Barton.
This is NPR News.

topics.text: Governor Hochul appoints State Attorney General James as special prosecutor for Cornell University gang rape investigation
Christa Pike survives lethal injection in Tennessee; Governor Lee halts executions pending third-party review
Over 2,500 doctors urge senators to reject Dr. Heidi Overton as FDA commissioner nominee
Maine Senate race between Susan Collins and Troy Jackson centers on gas and heating oil prices
Judge dismisses criminal case against former Olympian David Hearn for reflecting pool vandalism
Trump administration restores LGBTQ+ youth suicide prevention service through 988 Lifeline
Four astronauts arrive at International Space Station following SpaceX express eight-hour flight
